headline: Discussed student recommendations from the Summer Racial Justice Academy and ways to strengthen student support; no votes were recorded.
summary: Members and guests discussed recommendations from the Summer Racial Justice Academy and the district's Equity Collaborative. They also discussed student mental health, restorative practices, and access to social justice clubs. The minutes record no votes; they list action items for members to follow up.
decisions: A earlier district proposal to establish trusted adults in each school (equity advisors) was not approved.

decision_evidence.quote: The proposal was presented to the district but was not approved.

BSD Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Committee Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, October 13, 2026 at 6:00 PM 
Sustainability Academy - Library 123 North Street 
Commissioners Present: Polly Ericksen, Jeannie Waltz  
Staff Present: Autumn Bangora 
Guests: Students/SRJA Participants:  Ashley, Munira and Grace  
 
 
1. Opening  
1.1 Call meeting to order   
6:06pm  
1.2 Suspend Robert's Rules 
 
2. Public Comment 
None 
 
3. Discussion  
3.1 Autumn Bangoura presents the recommendations of the Summer Racial Justice 
Academy. Discussion of how these are moved into action by BSD. 
Guest students described their experience participating in SRJA; shared details 
developing recommendations and the capstone process used to identify and address 
equity issues within the school district. 
 Students begin by identifying broad topics/areas of concern, then ask why and 
continue to ask why as a way to  identify root causes/issues.  
 Then examine district data to better understand the issues. 
 Data sources include the district’s annual student survey and other presentations 
and reports addressing equity. 
 Students often conduct additional research or develop surveys to gather more 
information directly from students. 
 Students work in groups developing separate Capstone presentations outlining 
specific problems and potential recommendations for improvement. 
 The format of the capstone presentations has evolved. In recent years, students 
have moved toward more interactive presentations, including trifold type posters, 
which encouraged engagement and discussion with attendees. 
Participants discussed the importance of ensuring that student research and 
recommendations lead to meaningful changes in district practices and policies. 
  
Page 1 of 4
Draft
This led to a discussion about the District’s Equity Collaborative; Autumn shared details. 
 Entering its third year. 
 One of its primary purposes is to amplify student recommendations, particularly 
those developed through SRJA.  
 The collaborative was established in part because student recommendations were 
not always receiving sufficient attention or resulting in action. 
 The group includes representatives from each school site, along with staff and 
district leadership, including the superintendent. 
 In fall 2021, four SRJA students presented recommendations to the district 
virtually. 
 Following the presentation, school sites reviewed and discussed the 
recommendations. 
  
Autumn shared an existing tracker that documents progress on recommendations across 
multiple years .Recommendations from SRJA1-6 
 Notes indicate implementation status, including completed or addressed items, 
partially addressed items, and areas where further work is needed. 
Examples of areas where student recommendations have informed district work include: 
 Revising disciplinary processes and reducing suspensions. 
 Updating the student handbook. 
 Antiracist professional development. 
 Incorporating equity priorities into the district strategic plan. 
Mental health and student well-being continue to appear as recurring areas requiring 
attention. Participants noted that some recommendations remain unresolved despite 
progress in other areas.  
Discussion regarding the origins of the Sankofa Project influenced by an SRJA 
recommendation. Students shared much appreciation for African-American History 
teacher, Korey Whitfield's, leadership. 
Students departed–HUGE THANK YOU to Ashley, Munira and Grace!! 
Discussed how to create more meaningful opportunities for students to engage with 
district leadership and influence decisions. 
 Emphasized the importance of student participation being substantive rather than 
limited to organizing events or making presentations. 
o Ie: Collaboration between middle school and high school students, 
educators, and community partners 
Also discussed the growth of social justice clubs, including Youth Participatory Action 
Research (YPAR). 
Concerns were raised about the (un)availability of social justice clubs and Gender and 
Sexuality Alliances (GSAs) in some schools. Limited BSD staffing and capacity among 
community partners has made it difficult to provide staffing for all desired programs. 
After-school programming was discussed as one possible approach. 
  
Autumn shared info re: a former proposal to establish equity advisors in each school. 
Page 2 of 4
Draft
The proposed model would identify trusted adults whom students could approach when 
experiencing racism, discrimination, microaggressions, or bias in the classroom. Potential 
features included designated office hours and stipends to compensate staff for the 
additional responsibilities. 
The proposal was presented to the district but was not approved. The district's response 
was that designated employees already exist to receive reports of harassment (HHB). 
Group ”Yes and…” discussion included the following concerns and possibilities: 
 The existing structure may not adequately address the concerns students have 
shared, particularly when those concerns involve adult behavior, classroom 
interactions, or subtle forms of discrimination. 
 Students need trusted adults with whom they feel comfortable discussing difficult 
experiences–feel accessible to students and in an appropriate role to influence 
accountability. 
 The district should explore ways to make better use of existing staff and resources 
while identifying gaps in current support systems.  
Discussion re: “SRJA Recommendations and Progress” identifies student mental health as 
significant ongoing concerns: though it’s important to recognize that support services 
face substantial caseloads, addressing student mental health is more than additional 
hires..  
Key themes included: 
 Continues support of restorative practices; integrating student well-being into 
classroom practices; strengthening relationships between students and educators. 
 Providing teachers with training to respond effectively to emotional and 
behavioral needs. 
 Ensuring students can access appropriate spaces and support when overwhelmed. 
 Balancing student access to supportive spaces with expectations around 
classroom attendance and participation. 
Also discussed the impact of technology use.  
3.2 Teaching and Learning office: discuss how to request follow up regarding training in 
restorative practices and anti-racism. 
1. Equity tracker items to which this pertains under Leadership and Planning: 
a. Use the principles of equity to examine teaching practices. 
b. Providing anti-bias training for all staff. 
c. Implement Anti-racist lends to evaluation plans in order to hold all 
employees accountable. 
2. Discussed the board's responsibility for monitoring implementation of the 
district's equity policy. 
3. The conversation emphasized that equitable, high-quality curriculum alone is 
insufficient if students do not feel safe, supported, or included in their school 
communities. 
4. Key points included: 
5. Students' sense of belonging and mental health are foundational to successful 
learning. 
6. All teaching staff need appropriate training to understand trauma, mental health 
Page 3 of 4
Draft
needs, emotional regulation, and student behavior. 
7. Strong relationships between students and educators are essential. 
8. School principals play a critical role in establishing expectations and modeling 
equitable and restorative practices. 
9. School leadership must support staff in implementing the district's equity 
priorities. 
10. Professional development and teaching and learning initiatives should 
incorporate equity, student well-being, and trauma-informed practices.  
4. Action Items 
1. Jeannie -Review SRJA recommendations doc: Identify areas that remain incomplete in 
the context of the equity policy tracker (cross reference). 
2. Polly - Draft & share an email to the teaching and learning team to attend the next 
meeting (discuss equity tracker items ie: PD/training commitments/an update on 
implementation). 
3. Sparks & Jeannie - Give feedback/edit. 
4. Continue exploring student support mechanisms: Consider ways to improve students' 
access to trusted adults and reporting processes for microaggressions and bias. 
5. Continue monitoring student support needs: Keep IEP services, mental health needs, 
and trauma-informed training as areas for ongoing discussion.  
5. Adjournment 
6:53pm
